cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Share the roadway with people walking or blank riders and slow vehicles as well as passenger cars.
cards.back: Share the roadway with people walking or cycling, motorcycles, large trucks, animal riders and slow vehicles as well as passenger cars.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Use blank near schools, bus stops, playgrounds and parks, and remain prepared to yield.
cards.back: Use exceptional care around pedestrians, particularly near schools, bus stops, playgrounds and parks, and remain prepared to yield.

cards.back: A pedestrian in a crosswalk or crossing a driveway or alley entrance along a sidewalk has the stated right of way.

cards.back: Pedestrians should use intersection crosswalks, obey pedestrian controls and look in both directions before crossing.

cards.back: Without a sidewalk, pedestrians should walk along the left side facing approaching traffic.

cards.back: At night, a person walking should use white or light clothing or carry a light; walking on interstate or limited-access highways is prohibited.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Expect people to emerge between blank inspect the path for pedestrians before backing.
cards.back: Expect people to emerge between parked or stopped vehicles and inspect the path for pedestrians before backing.

cards.back: Comply with school-zone speed requirements when children or flashing school lights are present, and stop and yield when directed by a crossing guard.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Stop blank a white cane or harnessed guide dog is attempting to cross the road, and proceed afterward with particular care.
cards.back: Stop fully when a person with a white cane or harnessed guide dog is attempting to cross the road, and proceed afterward with particular care.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? A visually impaired pedestrian may blank stop before crossing; do not honk or shout at that pedestrian.
cards.back: A visually impaired pedestrian may listen for a vehicle to stop before crossing; do not honk or shout at that pedestrian.

cards.back: Bicycles using the road are vehicles whose riders share the traffic-law responsibilities, privileges and rights of motor-vehicle drivers.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? The passing-clearance rule treats blank feet as reasonable and prudent when motor traffic is moving at thirty miles per hour or less.
cards.back: The passing-clearance rule treats at least three feet as reasonable and prudent when motor traffic is moving at thirty miles per hour or less.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Above blank miles per hour, the bicycle-clearance requirement adds another foot for each additional ten miles per hour.
cards.back: Above thirty miles per hour, the bicycle-clearance requirement adds another foot for each additional ten miles per hour.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Yield blank where a bicycle path or lane crosses a road.
cards.back: Yield to bicyclists in intersections and where a bicycle path or lane crosses a road.

cards.back: Avoid sudden slowing or stops directly in front of a bicycle because a motor vehicle's stronger brakes can contribute to a collision.

cards.back: Do not sound a horn close to a bicyclist unless a collision threatens, since the sound may startle the rider into your path.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Watch for bicyclists entering blank from sidewalks into the road.
cards.back: Watch for bicyclists entering the lane, particularly children moving from sidewalks into the road.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Never blank a bicyclist's path or force the rider off the roadway.
cards.back: Never make a sharp turn across a bicyclist's path or force the rider off the roadway.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Although riders are blank, search for bicycles throughout the roadway rather than assuming each rider is correctly positioned.
cards.back: Although riders are required to follow traffic direction, search for bicycles throughout the roadway rather than assuming each rider is correctly positioned.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Rain, sand and gravel affect bicycles particularly strongly, so use blank surfaces.
cards.back: Rain, sand and gravel affect bicycles particularly strongly, so use extra caution when sharing those surfaces.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? A bicyclist normally signals turns and stops by hand but may blank; watch head movements or shoulder checks for additional clues.
cards.back: A bicyclist normally signals turns and stops by hand but may need both hands for control; watch head movements or shoulder checks for additional clues.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Before opening a parked vehicle's door blank rear areas for bicycles, especially near homes or schools.
cards.back: Before opening a parked vehicle's door or backing, check side and rear areas for bicycles, especially near homes or schools.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Motorcyclists have the same roadway rights and responsibilities as other drivers but their narrow profile can blank and complicate speed judgments.
cards.back: Motorcyclists have the same roadway rights and responsibilities as other drivers but their narrow profile can hide them in blind spots and complicate speed judgments.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Give a motorcycle the entire lane and do blank it within that lane.
cards.back: Give a motorcycle the entire lane and do not attempt to travel beside it within that lane.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Before turning left across opposing blank and judge its approach speed.
cards.back: Before turning left across opposing traffic, carefully identify any motorcycle and judge its approach speed.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Leave blank seconds of following time behind a motorcycle.
cards.back: Leave at least four seconds of following time behind a motorcycle.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Confirm that a motorcyclist is blank on an operating turn signal, since it may not cancel automatically.
cards.back: Confirm that a motorcyclist is actually turning rather than relying on an operating turn signal, since it may not cancel automatically.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Bad weather and slippery surfaces may blank speed or course, and wet-road glare can be particularly difficult at night.
cards.back: Bad weather and slippery surfaces may cause a motorcyclist to change speed or course, and wet-road glare can be particularly difficult at night.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Crosswinds and air blasts from fast large trucks can blank on bridges or exposed highway stretches.
cards.back: Crosswinds and air blasts from fast large trucks can shift a motorcycle's path, especially on bridges or exposed highway stretches.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Uneven pavement, gravel, debris, seams, grooves or covers can blank or grated bridge surfaces may cause wobbling.
cards.back: Uneven pavement, gravel, debris, seams, grooves or covers can affect a motorcycle's travel; metal or grated bridge surfaces may cause wobbling.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? A rear orange-and-red reflective or fluorescent triangle marks an animal-drawn, farm or construction vehicle traveling below blank miles per hour.
cards.back: A rear orange-and-red reflective or fluorescent triangle marks an animal-drawn, farm or construction vehicle traveling below twenty-five miles per hour.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Approach a slow vehicle blank ensuring the maneuver is safe.
cards.back: Approach a slow vehicle carefully and pass only after ensuring the maneuver is safe.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Watch rural roads for farm machinery crossing or moving along the highway and do blank hear your approach.
cards.back: Watch rural roads for farm machinery crossing or moving along the highway and do not expect its operator to hear your approach.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Animal-drawn vehicles and horse blank traffic-rule duties with motor vehicles.
cards.back: Animal-drawn vehicles and horse riders share road-use rights and traffic-rule duties with motor vehicles.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Near a horse, slow down, assess blank without sounding the horn or revving the engine.
cards.back: Near a horse, slow down, assess the situation and pass carefully without sounding the horn or revving the engine.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Large commercial vehicles maneuver less easily blank larger blind spots and longer acceleration and stopping distances.
cards.back: Large commercial vehicles maneuver less easily than cars and generally have larger blind spots and longer acceleration and stopping distances.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? A large truck or bus needs blank enough space for its maneuver.
cards.back: A large truck or bus needs additional turning room, so leave enough space for its maneuver.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? The no-zone means blank blind areas where a truck or bus driver cannot see nearby vehicles.
cards.back: The no-zone means the front, rear and side blind areas where a truck or bus driver cannot see nearby vehicles.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? A truck's right-side blind area can blank extend along the vehicle's full length; avoid staying beside it longer than necessary.
cards.back: A truck's right-side blind area can begin behind the cab and extend along the vehicle's full length; avoid staying beside it longer than necessary.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? If the truck driver's face is blank mirror, assume the driver cannot see your vehicle.
cards.back: If the truck driver's face is not visible in the side mirror, assume the driver cannot see your vehicle.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? The handbook's ideal-condition example gives a loaded truck at blank miles per hour at least three hundred thirty-five feet to stop, even with good tires and adjusted brakes.
cards.back: The handbook's ideal-condition example gives a loaded truck at fifty-five miles per hour at least three hundred thirty-five feet to stop, even with good tires and adjusted brakes.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Avoid blank lanes close in front of a large vehicle because it needs more distance to stop.
cards.back: Avoid entering the road or changing lanes close in front of a large vehicle because it needs more distance to stop.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? After passing a large vehicle, wait until blank your rearview mirror before returning ahead of it and maintaining speed.
cards.back: After passing a large vehicle, wait until its full front appears in your rearview mirror before returning ahead of it and maintaining speed.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Rear blind spots behind a large vehicle may extend as far as blank feet, so avoid close following and position where its side mirrors can reveal your vehicle.
cards.back: Rear blind spots behind a large vehicle may extend as far as two hundred feet, so avoid close following and position where its side mirrors can reveal your vehicle.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Where practical, avoid blank exits or steep hills to give slow large vehicles room to join or use that lane.
cards.back: Where practical, avoid the right lane near weigh-station exits or steep hills to give slow large vehicles room to join or use that lane.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? A truck or bus may blank turn and use space in adjoining lanes; never squeeze between it and the curb.
cards.back: A truck or bus may swing left before a right turn and use space in adjoining lanes; never squeeze between it and the curb.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Wait until the large vehicle blank trying to turn through its maneuvering space.
cards.back: Wait until the large vehicle completes its turn instead of trying to turn through its maneuvering space.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? When meeting an oncoming truck, keep blank reduce side-contact risk and the effect of air turbulence between vehicles.
cards.back: When meeting an oncoming truck, keep safely to the right to reduce side-contact risk and the effect of air turbulence between vehicles.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? If uncertain about an approaching truck's or bus's speed, do blank path because it needs more stopping room than a car.
cards.back: If uncertain about an approaching truck's or bus's speed, do not turn left across its path because it needs more stopping room than a car.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Stop blank so that a turning large vehicle has the room the marking preserves.
cards.back: Stop behind the marked intersection line so that a turning large vehicle has the room the marking preserves.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Never cut off a large vehicle to reach a turn or exit or to get ahead of it at a blank-lane construction area.
cards.back: Never cut off a large vehicle to reach a turn or exit or to get ahead of it at a one-lane construction area.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Yield blank a siren or flashing lights from any direction by moving right and stopping without obstructing an intersection.
cards.back: Yield to an emergency vehicle using a siren or flashing lights from any direction by moving right and stopping without obstructing an intersection.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? After the emergency vehicle passes, signal before reentering the roadway and do blank.
cards.back: After the emergency vehicle passes, signal before reentering the roadway and do so only when safe.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Keep blank feet behind a fire truck using warning lights or a siren, and do not drive or park in the block where it has stopped for a fire alarm.
cards.back: Keep at least five hundred feet behind a fire truck using warning lights or a siren, and do not drive or park in the block where it has stopped for a fire alarm.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? At a highway emergency, traffic stop blank, reduce speed and provide a wide berth when practical without endangering opposing traffic.
cards.back: At a highway emergency, traffic stop or stopped vehicle displaying warnings, reduce speed and provide a wide berth when practical without endangering opposing traffic.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? When traffic allows it safely, move into a lane away from the incident or emergency personnel and promptly leave a lane that is blank.
cards.back: When traffic allows it safely, move into a lane away from the incident or emergency personnel and promptly leave a lane that is wholly or partly blocked.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Follow authorized traffic directions and blank, fire, maintenance activity or other roadway emergency.
cards.back: Follow authorized traffic directions and emergency signals around a crash, fire, maintenance activity or other roadway emergency.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? A move-over-law violation brings a fine and penalty assessment, with a larger fine for another offense blank months.
cards.back: A move-over-law violation brings a fine and penalty assessment, with a larger fine for another offense within twelve months.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? For a police traffic stop, blank select park; stay inside unless the officer requests that you leave.
cards.back: For a police traffic stop, pull aside, stop fully and select park; stay inside unless the officer requests that you leave.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Switch off the engine, activate hazard blank the interior during the described police stop.

cards.back: When an officer requests license and registration documents, explain where they are before reaching slowly while keeping one hand on the wheel.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? For an unmarked police vehicle, check that its blue lights are blank uniform can be asked for a badge or department identification.
cards.back: For an unmarked police vehicle, check that its blue lights are activated; an officer without a uniform can be asked for a badge or department identification.

cards.front: Which words replace the blank in this handbook rule? Work zones can blank and moving machinery, creating hazards from narrow lanes and rough pavement.
cards.back: Work zones can involve closed lanes, detours, workers and moving machinery, creating hazards from narrow lanes and rough pavement.

cards.back: Use exceptional caution at night in a work zone even when no workers are visible.

cards.back: Adjust lane position to leave room for workers and construction equipment and follow the posted work-zone instructions.

cards.back: Do not return to normal speed until the End Road Work sign is visible.

cards.back: Plan for work-zone delays, depart early and use an alternate route when one is available.
